# Getting started {#sec-start}

biyos is a C library with a C++ core. A program uses it through one C header, and a Python package calls the same library.

## Building {#sec-start-build}

biyos needs CMake 3.25 or later and a compiler for C99 and C++20. It is tested with GCC on Ubuntu 24.04, Clang on macOS 15 and MSVC on Windows Server 2022. From a clone of the repository:

```sh
cmake -S library -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

The configure step downloads GoogleTest for the tests. Three options change the build:

| Option | Default | Effect |
| ------------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` | `ON` | build `biyos` as a shared library; `OFF` builds a static one |
| `BIYOS_BUILD_TESTS` | `ON` | build the tests and register them with CTest |
| `BIYOS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` | `OFF` | treat every compiler warning as an error |

The library lands in `build/lib`, except `biyos.dll` on Windows, which lands in `build/bin`. Visual Studio adds a folder named for the configuration. The header is in `library/include/biyos`.

To install the library, the header and a CMake package into a prefix:

```sh
cmake --install build --prefix "$PWD/install"
```

The examples are a project of their own, built and tested against that prefix:

```sh
cmake -S examples -B build/examples -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/install"
cmake --build build/examples
ctest --test-dir build/examples --output-on-failure
```

## The library and its header {#sec-start-layers}

A program includes one header, `biyos/biyos.h`, which needs only `<stddef.h>` and `<stdint.h>`. The library exports the functions of that header and nothing else, so no C++ type or exception reaches the caller.

![The layers of biyos. Each arrow points from a part to one it uses. Only `biyos.h` crosses the library's boundary.](../figures/layers.svg){#fig-layers}

## A first program {#sec-start-program}

This program prints the version of the library, then creates an environment and frees it:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/start.c"}
```

An environment holds the options, the events and the last error of each thread. Every model is made on one. Every call returns `BIYOS_OK` when it succeeds ([Errors](#sec-errors)).

### With CMake

A CMake project finds an installed biyos as a package, of exactly the version it was built as:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(app LANGUAGES C)

find_package(biyos 0.1.0 EXACT CONFIG REQUIRED)

add_executable(app app.c)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE biyos::biyos)
```

Configure it with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$PWD/install`. The target `biyos::biyos` brings the include directory and, for a static build, the definition `BIYOS_STATIC` that Windows needs.

### Without CMake

On Linux, compile against the header and link the library from the build tree:

```sh
cc -std=c99 start.c -I biyos/include -L biyos/build/lib -lbiyos \
   -Wl,-rpath,"$PWD/biyos/build/lib" -o start
./start
```

It prints `biyos 0.1.0`.

## From Python {#sec-start-python}

The Python package needs Python 3.10 or later and nothing else at run time. It builds against an installed biyos of the same version, a shared Release build as above, and keeps its own copy of the library:

```sh
CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/install" python -m pip install ./interfaces/python
```

It calls the C API through `ctypes`, so every rule of this book holds in Python too. The first program becomes:

```{.python file="examples/code/python/start.py"}
```

The `with` block frees the environment when it ends. `pytest examples/test/python` runs every Python example. [The Python package](#sec-python) covers the rest.
